hi there, im new to lavan and need some help to read my results.
im using sem int he contect of the theory of planned behaviour.
i have some questions, hopefully someone can provide me some insights:
in my process i have


1- is it correct to have 3 models to unobserved variables and then use these to predict another one? and use this observed variable in a second regression? att_x, pbc_x and soc_x are not observed
  Intention_100   ~ Att_x + PBC_x + Soc_x
  beh_avg     ~ Intention_100 + PBC_x   + PANT + dist_org_100
2- how can i know if my model is fitting correctly?
3- I want to extract the equation that describes intention_100 and beh_avg,
can i extract the equation that describes these variables?
4- What is the difference between the standardized solution and the one from the output? are the standardized solutions the same as proportions?
5-  What do you think about the number of observations? would you consider these results valid?
6- what tests should i run to see if my model is doing ok?

thanks a lot in advance!
j

Sorry, I don't understand your questions. Maybe others understand your questions, then again sorry. You fit one model and not 3 models. You can determine the model fit with the usual for measures. Maybe it makes sense to post these questions on SEMnet?

Von: lav...@googlegroups.com <lav...@googlegroups.com> im Auftrag von Jonathan Cohen <cohen...@gmail.com>
Gesendet: Dienstag, 9. Mai 2023, 19:09
An: lavaan <lav...@googlegroups.com>
Betreff: interpreation of results

hi there, im new to lavan and need some help to read my results.
im using sem int he contect of the theory of planned behaviour.
i have some questions, hopefully someone can provide me some insights:
in my process i have


1- is it correct to have 3 models to unobserved variables and then use these to predict another one? and use this observed variable in a second regression? att_x, pbc_x and soc_x are not observed
  Intention_100   ~ Att_x + PBC_x + Soc_x
  beh_avg     ~ Intention_100 + PBC_x   + PANT + dist_org_100
2- how can i know if my model is fitting correctly?
3- I want to extract the equation that describes intention_100 and beh_avg,
can i extract the equation that describes these variables?
4- What is the difference between the standardized solution and the one from the output? are the standardized solutions the same as proportions?
5-  What do you think about the number of observations? would you consider these results valid?
6- what tests should i run to see if my model is doing ok?

thanks a lot in advance!
j

On Tue, 9 May 2023 at 10:09, Jonathan Cohen <cohen...@gmail.com> wrote:
[snip[

1- is it correct to have 3 models to unobserved variables and then use these to predict another one? and use this observed variable in a second regression? att_x, pbc_x and soc_x are not observed
  Intention_100   ~ Att_x + PBC_x + Soc_x
  beh_avg     ~ Intention_100 + PBC_x   + PANT + dist_org_100

I think by three models, you mean three latent variables?  You are not fitting three models (although you could fit them separately), you are fitting one model simultaneously.

If so, yes, this is correct.
2- how can i know if my model is fitting correctly?

Books have been written on this subject. I wouldn't say your model fits correctly, I would say your model fits the data. That is, the data generating process that your model hypothesizes can reproduce the data that you have. This

3- I want to extract the equation that describes intention_100 and beh_avg,
can i extract the equation that describes these variables?
Is that the regression? This is in the regression parameters.
4- What is the difference between the standardized solution and the one from the output? are the standardized solutions the same as proportions?
I'm not sure what you mean by this.
5-  What do you think about the number of observations? would you consider these results valid?

The number of observations is on the low side, but the model does seem to fit OK.  The indicators generally seem to be highly reliable which can compensate to some extent for a smaller sample size. 

But the parameters in the structural model, which is probably the part you're interested in, are generally not significant. Your small sample means you can't draw a lot of conclusions from that. 

Validity is not a statistical feature of a model. I don't know anything about your data - maybe you made them up. :)  In which case it's not valid, but I wouldn't know that. :)
6- what tests should i run to see if my model is doing ok?

I'm not sure what you mean by tests. 

One thing you might want to consider is that the variances of your variables are pretty different. A rule of thumb that's sometimes given is that your variances should be approximately within an order of magnitude. You can divide your variables by 10 (or 100) to make the variances more similar 

A couple of other things I noticed:

 ATT_hygenc_100 has a negative loading, where all others are positive. Is that expected?

You have a lot of correlated errors - in particular self_1_100 is correlated with 4 other indicators.  Two of them are indicators of the same factor, two are indicators of different factors. Why did you add these? Were they specified in advance? Did you use the modification indices?  Intention_100 is regression on three latent variables (IIUC) and also correlated with a variable that is an indicator of a latent variable.

A path diagram would make it clearer what's happening. 
 
Hope that helps,

Jeremy

thanks a lot in advance!
j

Thanks for your quick and useful answers.
I used modification index to reach a better fix. i only took covariance when they were relevant.
Indeed, im mostly interested in extracting "the equations" that describe beh_avg and intention. These equations will be used in a simulation, and that is my main aim, but i want to make sure that I'm taking the right coefficients. For a regression analysis i know how to construct the relationship that explains my dependent variable, but here i found it a bit more complex, specially to describe how these variables relate to each other.
1- So would you say that my non-observed variable could be estimated via something like this?:
Att_x =~  ATT_good_100  * 12.126   + ATT_mprtnt_100  * 13.036  + self_1_100* 7.951 + self_2_100 *9.216   + ATT_useful_100 *   8.591   
Should i include an intercept term? where can i find it?

here is my path diagram

On Wednesday, May 10, 2023 at 6:10:25 AM UTC+2 jeremy...@gmail.com wrote:


On Tue, 9 May 2023 at 10:09, Jonathan Cohen <cohen...@gmail.com> wrote:
[snip[
 
1- is it correct to have 3 models to unobserved variables and then use these to predict another one? and use this observed variable in a second regression? att_x, pbc_x and soc_x are not observed
  Intention_100   ~ Att_x + PBC_x + Soc_x
  beh_avg     ~ Intention_100 + PBC_x   + PANT + dist_org_100

I think by three models, you mean three latent variables?  You are not fitting three models (although you could fit them separately), you are fitting one model simultaneously.

If so, yes, this is correct. 

 

2- how can i know if my model is fitting correctly?

Books have been written on this subject. I wouldn't say your model fits correctly, I would say your model fits the data. That is, the data generating process that your model hypothesizes can reproduce the data that you have. This 
 
3- I want to extract the equation that describes intention_100 and beh_avg,
can i extract the equation that describes these variables?

Is that the regression? This is in the regression parameters. 
 
4- What is the difference between the standardized solution and the one from the output? are the standardized solutions the same as proportions?

I'm not sure what you mean by this. 
 
5-  What do you think about the number of observations? would you consider these results valid?

The number of observations is on the low side, but the model does seem to fit OK.  The indicators generally seem to be highly reliable which can compensate to some extent for a smaller sample size. 

But the parameters in the structural model, which is probably the part you're interested in, are generally not significant. Your small sample means you can't draw a lot of conclusions from that. 

Validity is not a statistical feature of a model. I don't know anything about your data - maybe you made them up. :)  In which case it's not valid, but I wouldn't know that. :) 
 

6- what tests should i run to see if my model is doing ok?


I'm not sure what you mean by tests. 

One thing you might want to consider is that the variances of your variables are pretty different. A rule of thumb that's sometimes given is that your variances should be approximately within an order of magnitude. You can divide your variables by 10 (or 100) to make the variances more similar 

A couple of other things I noticed:

 ATT_hygenc_100 has a negative loading, where all others are positive. Is that expected?

You have a lot of correlated errors - in particular self_1_100 is correlated with 4 other indicators.  Two of them are indicators of the same factor, two are indicators of different factors. Why did you add these? Were they specified in advance? Did you use the modification indices?  Intention_100 is regression on three latent variables (IIUC) and also correlated with a variable that is an indicator of a latent variable.

A path diagram would make it clearer what's happening. 
 
Hope that helps,

Jeremy

parts:
Jonathan,
Jeremy did a great job of decoding your questions.  Here are a few additional reactions.

I believe what you had in mind when you wrote that you had three models was that you have three exogenous latent variables each of which has a reflective measurement model.  However, you also have an endogenous latent variable that also has a reflective measurement model.  Once these are combined into one SE model, we are more inclined to think of them as one measurement model with four latent variables.  So, the clearest way to write about this is probably to describe the number of latent variables.

Regarding fit, I would suggest that you read the two chapters on local fit and global fit in Rex Kline's SEM text.  You can never know your model is fitting correctly because this is always an ampliative inference that goes beyond your data.  However, there are a number of things you can look at that will help you make this judgment in a systematic way.

Please be aware that lavaan syntax if case sensitive.  So Att_x and att_x are potentially distinct variables in a model.

The equations in the model are specified by your model syntax and can be made specific by substituting in the parameter estimates.  If this is not clear from the tabled output, you can use lavInspect to request the estimates in matrix form.  However, it could be that you are looking for something that is not there.  In regression, you can plug in an observed predictor variable and compute a predicted value for an outcome variable.  In your SE model, the exogenous variables are the latent variables, not the observed indicators of them.  So, there is no analogous process of plugging in values for the observed x variables and obtaining predicted values for the observed y variables.  Instead, you would begin your simulation with the exogenous latent variables, and use the simulated values to then simulate both the observed x variables and the endogenous latent variables, which you would then use to simulate the observed y variables.  However, the built-in simulateData() function uses a more general method of first deriving the model-implied covariance matrix of the observed variables and then simulating all of them directly from this joint distribution.

When you refer to the solution in the output, I think that you mean the raw (unstandardized) solution.  You can request that all standardized estimates be included in the output as well.  One option is that the model is rescaled so that all the latent variables are z scores.  Another option is that the model is rescaled so that all the variables are z scores.  (This is analogous to the idea in OLS regression that if you analyze z scores then b = beta.)

The current issue of Psychological Methods includes a tutorial on evaluating sample size in SEM.

If you data contains outliers or other influential observations, you can do a sensitivity analysis by running the model with these cases removed and with them included.  However, for the most part, you will find what you need included in the available output from when you fit the model.

If you wish to include intercepts, see the page on mean structures in the Lavaan online tutorial.

In a simulation, you need to include the random disturbance as a draw from a random distribution or all of your cases with the same predictors will have the same value.  However, unless you have a good reason not to, consider using the built in simulation function.
